title: Making Smart Homes Fit for Autistic Children: Family Work and Monitored Independence
abstract: arXiv:2610.38008v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: General-purpose smart-home technologies are increasingly present in family life, yet how they support or disrupt autistic children and families with autistic children remains underexamined. We conducted a multi-source qualitative study drawing on five caregiver interviews, Xiaohongshu (also known internationally as RedNote) posts explicitly situated in autism contexts, and contextual posts from Xiaohongshu and Weibo. We find that families create support for autistic children by adapting environmental outputs, prompts, and interaction channels, while sensory intensity, communicative rules, and opaque operating states can turn the same technologies into barriers. Support also depends on continuing family work, including translation, configuration, modification, maintenance, and boundary-setting. translated_title: 让智能家居适配自闭症儿童：家庭劳动与受监护的独立性
translated_abstract: 通用型智能家居技术日益融入家庭生活，然而它们如何支持或干扰自闭症儿童及有自闭症儿童的家庭，仍缺乏充分研究。我们开展了一项多来源的质性研究，数据来源包括五次照护者访谈、明确处于自闭症语境下的小红书（RedNote）帖文，以及来自小红书和微博的情境性帖文。研究发现，家庭通过调整环境输出、提示方式和交互渠道来为自闭症儿童创造支持，而感官刺激强度、交流规则和不透明的运行状态则可能使同样的技术成为障碍。这种支持还依赖于持续的家庭劳动，包括翻译、配置、改造、维护和边界设定。远程监控在实现“有条件的独立性”的同时，也引发了安全、隐私与控制之间的张力。我们贡献了三个概念……（摘要截断）
tldr: 该研究通过质性分析发现，有自闭症儿童的家庭需依靠持续的家庭劳动（翻译、配置、改造、维护与边界设定）来调适智能家居技术，使其从障碍变为支持，而远程监控则在安全、隐私与控制之间产生张力并带来一种“受监护的独立性”。
en_tdlr: Through a multi-source qualitative study, this paper shows that families of autistic children rely on ongoing family work—translation, configuration, modification, maintenance, and boundary-setting—to turn smart-home technologies into supports rather than barriers, while remote monitoring enables a form of "monitored independence" marked by tensions among safety, privacy, and control.
